question: Does an ACCUMULATED candidate territory beat a single candidate fragment as the occupancy comparison target?
script: scratchpad/accum.py (three arms over one shared field)
framing_note: Deployment shape: a NEW fragment q arrives and is matched to identity THREADS built only from fragments with end < q.start. This is the reverse of matchlab_core/reid/episodes.py, which admits FUTURE fragments as candidates. Field size here is ~11 threads, not ~550 fragments, so rank-1 is NOT comparable to the six-arm ablation table.
threading: oracle (GT player_id) -- this is a CEILING on what a two-pass bootstrap could deliver, not an achievable number

arms.recent: candidate = its most recent prior fragment (equivalent to today's fragment-vs-fragment design)
arms.longest: candidate = its longest prior fragment (control: is any gain merely 'more frames'?)
arms.accum: candidate = ALL its prior fragments pooled

finding: Accumulation wins on all 6 halves: +7.4 rank-1 over the current fragment-vs-fragment design and +6.6 over the longest-prior-fragment control, so the gain is accumulation and not merely more observed frames. AUC +0.030. This restores the justification for the two-pass bootstrap that was dropped earlier.
